note: Game content for the banking career: original puzzles, interview questions, training quizzes and workday scenarios. All characters and situations are fictional.

aptitude.q: A customer deposits ₦45,000 and withdraws ₦12,500. What is the net change?
A loan of ₦100,000 at 10% simple interest for 2 years costs how much interest?
If all tellers are staff, and some staff are managers, then…
Which word is closest in meaning to 'prudent'?
₦1,550 to the dollar: how many naira is $40?
A branch serves 240 customers in 8 hours. How many per hour?
Ada is older than Bayo. Chidi is younger than Bayo. Who is youngest?
A fee rises from ₦50 to ₦65. What is the percentage increase?
₦250,000 shared in the ratio 3:2 gives the larger share as…
If 4 tellers clear a queue in 30 minutes, how long would 6 tellers take (same pace)?
A customer's balance is −₦3,000 after a ₦10,000 withdrawal. What was it before?

a.t: A short story: my studies, what I've done to earn and learn, and why banking now.
I'm hardworking, honest and a fast learner.
Everything from primary school until today, in detail.
My uncle works here, so I know the bank well.

interview.q: A customer insists on a product that you know doesn't suit them. What do you do?

a.t: Explain the risks clearly, suggest what fits, and record that they were advised.
Sell it: they asked, and it helps my target.
Refuse to serve them.
Ask my supervisor to decide.

interview.q: Why do you want to work here?

a.t: I've read about what you do and where you're going, and here's where I fit.
Banks pay well.
I applied everywhere.
My family wants me in a bank.

interview.q: Your teammate is taking cash from the till. What do you do?

a.t: Report it through the proper channel, even if it's uncomfortable.
Talk to them privately and keep it between us.
Ignore it. Not my business.
Ask for a share.

interview.q: Describe a time you worked under pressure.

a.t: The situation, what I did, and the result, with numbers.
I always work well under pressure.
I don't really get pressured.
During exams, I read all night.

interview.q: Where do you see yourself in five years?

a.t: Skilled in my track, trusted with more, and ready to lead a team.
In your seat.
Abroad, honestly.
I haven't thought about it.

interview.q: What would you do if you made a mistake that cost a customer money?

a.t: Own it, tell my supervisor, fix it for the customer and log it so it doesn't repeat.
Fix it quietly before anyone notices.
Blame the system.
Hope the customer doesn't notice.

interview.q: Do you have any questions for us?

a.t: What does success look like in the first six months in this role?
How much is the salary?
No questions.
How soon can I be promoted?

practical.ops: Reconcile today's ledger against the statement and find the mismatch.
practical.cs: Handle a difficult customer request correctly.
practical.rm: Advise a customer on a product, suitably.

training.q: A customer can't explain where a large cash deposit came from. You should…
a: Ask, record, and escalate it under AML procedure
Tell the customer you're reporting them
Selling a product that doesn't suit the customer
A second person checks key transactions
Buys the asset and sells it to you at an agreed mark-up

training.q: A debt-to-income ratio of 60% suggests the borrower is…
A colleague asks for your login 'just for today'. You…
a: Refuse and remind them of policy

training.q: Good feedback to a team member is…

a: A loss from failed processes, people, systems or outside events

training.q: Before approving a loan, the most important check is…
a: Whether the branch target is met

requests.ask: "My pension came in, but the app says the money is not there. My grandson says I've been scammed."

a.t: Check her statement with her, show the credit, and help her set up her app safely.
Tell her to call the call centre.
Offer her a fixed deposit while she's here.

requests.ask: "I want to break my fixed deposit early. My shop needs stock."

a.t: Explain the early-break charge and options (like a deposit-backed loan), then let him choose.
Break it immediately without explaining charges.
Refuse: it's not due yet.

requests.ask: "Someone called saying they're from the bank and asked for my OTP. I gave it. Now ₦40,000 is gone!"

a.t: Block the card and app now, log a fraud claim, and explain how to stay safe.
Tell her it's her fault for sharing the OTP.
Promise she'll get the money back today.

requests.ask: "I'll open an account with ₦50 million today if you skip the ID checks. I'm in a hurry."

a.t: Politely insist on full KYC. A big deposit doesn't change the rules.
Open it now and collect the documents later.
Send him away.

requests.ask: "Can I get a loan for my wedding? My salary comes into this account."

a.t: Check her income and existing debts, and offer what she can comfortably repay.
Offer the maximum: bigger loan, bigger target.
Tell her weddings are a waste of money.

requests.ask: "My son wants me to put all my savings in a crypto plan he saw. Should I move my money through your bank?"

a.t: Explain the risks of unregulated investments, and offer to show regulated options.
Process the transfer; it's his money.
Sell him the bank's highest-fee investment fund instead.

tickets.t: The mobile app crashes for every user on one Android version since last night's release.
a: Roll back the release and fix it in testing

tickets.t: A branch printer won't print customer statements. Other branches are fine.
a: Check the branch printer's driver and queue

tickets.t: Transfers are timing out between 9 and 10 a.m. every day.
a: Check capacity and queues at peak hours
Tell customers to transfer at night

tickets.t: A staff member says they clicked a link in an email and now their screen is locked with a ransom note.
a: Isolate the computer from the network and alert security
Forward the email to colleagues as a warning

tickets.t: The daily report shows 0 transactions for a busy branch.
a: Check the data feed from that branch before trusting the report

supervision.t: Two tellers are off sick and the queue is out of the door.

a.t: Move a back-office officer to the counter and open the express queue for deposits.
Tell customers to come back tomorrow.
Make the remaining tellers skip the second check on cash.

supervision.t: Your best officer has missed their target for the first time and looks worried.

a.t: Talk privately, find out why, and agree a plan together.
Warn them in front of the team.
Ignore it; one bad month is fine.

supervision.t: A team member is pushing customers into products to hit targets.

a.t: Stop it, review the sales, and retrain them on suitability.
Let it go: the numbers look good.
Transfer them to another branch.

supervision.t: Two staff want the same leave week during the festive season.

a.t: Agree a fair rule (like who asked first, or rotating years) and explain it.
Give it to your favourite.
Cancel both.

learning.q: {bank} invests heavily in training. What will you do with it?

a.t: Use every module, apply it on the job, and teach what I learn to the next intake.
Learn as much as I can.
Pass the exams.
Training is boring; I learn on the job.

stability.q: {bank} has served customers for generations. How would you respect that while improving things?

a.t: Learn why things are done as they are, then suggest small, tested improvements.
Follow the rules.
Modernise everything quickly.
Old banks need shaking up.

digital.q: Our customers live on their phones. How would you make {bank}'s app better?

a.t: Watch where customers get stuck, fix the biggest pain first, and measure it.
Add more features.
Copy what other apps do.
I don't really use banking apps.

pan_african.q: {bank} works across many countries. How would you serve a customer trading across borders?

a.t: Understand their trade cycle and currencies, then offer the right payment and trade products.
Open them a domiciliary account.
Refer them to another branch.
Tell them to use cash.

sales.q: {bank} has ambitious business targets. How do you hit yours without cutting corners?

a.t: Know my customers well, offer what genuinely fits, and never trade compliance for a sale.
Work long hours.
Push the products with the best commission.
Whatever it takes.

growth.q: {bank} is growing fast. How do you handle constant change?

a.t: Stay organised, ask questions early, and help new colleagues settle in.
I adapt.
I prefer things to stay the same.
I'll leave if it's too much.

service.q: A customer has waited 40 minutes and is angry. You're the next free officer at {bank}. What do you do?

a.t: Apologise sincerely, fix their issue, then flag what caused the delay.
Serve them quickly.
Ask them to calm down first.
Tell them everyone has been waiting.

sectors.q: {bank} focuses on health, education, agriculture, energy and transport. Which interests you, and why?

a.t: Pick one, give a real example of its financing needs, and how the bank could help.
All of them.
The one that pays most.
I don't mind.

wealth.q: A client of {bank} wants to grow their savings safely. What do you ask first?

a.t: Their goals, timeline and risk tolerance, before suggesting anything.
How much they have.
Whether they've heard of our funds.
Nothing; I'd show the top-performing fund.

global.q: {bank} follows global compliance standards. A big client wants an exception 'just this once'. Your answer?

a.t: No exceptions: explain the rule, offer what's possible, and escalate if needed.
Ask my manager.
Allow it if it's small.
Big clients get exceptions.

merger.q: {bank} has just merged two banks. How would you help two teams become one?

a.t: Learn both ways of working, keep customers informed, and build trust with new colleagues.
Do my own job well.
Stick with my old team.
Wait and see who stays.

ethics.q: At a non-interest bank like {bank}, how is financing different from a conventional loan?

a.t: It's trade or partnership based, like Murabaha, with the profit agreed upfront and no interest.
It's interest-free.
It's the same with a different name.
I'm not sure.

field.q: {bank} serves small traders and farmers. How would you assess a market woman with no payslip?

a.t: Visit her business, look at her daily sales and records, and talk to her group members.
Ask for a payslip.
Lend small and hope.
Decline: no payslip, no loan.

projects.q: {bank} finances big projects for national development. What makes a project worth funding?

a.t: Clear demand, a sound plan, capable promoters, and cash flows that can repay.
If the government supports it.
If it's big.
If the promoter is well connected.
